mechanics.operation_0: Store the second stack word directly at position offset 0x14.
mechanics.operation_1: Add the second stack word to the old position and store the 32-bit result.
mechanics.operation_2: Add the second stack word to capacity offset 0x10 and store the 32-bit result.
mechanics.unknown_operation: Leave the old position in place, then apply the same capacity validation to that unchanged position.
mechanics.within_capacity: Return true when the resulting position is less than or equal to capacity.
mechanics.disabled_resize: When the resulting position exceeds capacity and resize_enabled is zero, store capacity at position and return false.
mechanics.enabled_resize: When the flag is nonzero, call the observed thiscall resize boundary with the resulting position as the requested capacity.
mechanics.resize_failure: If the boundary returns false, restore the old position and return false; if it returns true, retain the resulting position and return true.

evidence.observation: Ghidra reports IO::MemoryStream::Write with body range 0x0093c0c0-0x0093c12b and 45 instructions.

The disassembly preserves ECX as stream, reads two stack words, handles raw operation values 0, 1, and 2, stores position, compares against capacity, checks the byte flag at 0x18, and returns AL with RET 8.
Ghidra reports two direct caller functions, 0x0041c1d0 and 0x00902d40.
Ghidra reports six xrefs including the three direct call sites and data references at 0x0143cb10, 0x0143eba0, and 0x00811d32.
The resize boundary receives the stream in ECX and a requested capacity in the stack, returns a byte, and owns the external buffer replacement and refcount transition.
The imported structure is 36 bytes with position at 0x14, capacity at 0x10, and resize_enabled at 0x18.
